summary: The earlier grease branch now succeeds. The first remaining divergence is the turn after greasing the hands: C allmain.c calls do_wear.c:glibr() while Glib is active, and glibr() reports the unwielded quarterstaff slipping, clears the wield slot, and drops it. That second message makes the TTY wait at step 18; js/allmain.js omits the elapsed-turn glibr call, so the grease message has no --More-- marker and the quarterstaff drop never occurs.

source.branch: On the elapsed turn after apply.c:use_grease() grants Glib to the ungloved hands, do_wear.c:glibr() runs. With no slipping rings or offhand weapon, the active branch is the primary weapon arm: the Wizard is wielding a non-AKLYS, unwelded quarterstaff, so glibr() prints the slip message, clears uwep with setuwep(NULL), and drops the staff through dropx().

Upstream reachability: apply.c:doapply -> use_grease() -> potion.c:make_glib() activates Glib for the hands; the next paid turn reaches allmain.c:moveloop_core -> glibr().
dependencies: Preserve all glibr branches and shared equipment state: uarmg gates ring slipping; uleft/uright, uswapwep, u.twoweap, uwep, welded(), bimanual(), canletgo(), Ring_off(), setuswapwep(), and setuwep() determine which items fall and in what message order.

The reachable quarterstaff branch uses do_wear.c weapon naming and otense helpers, clears the wield slot before do.c:dropx(), then follows the ordinary floor-drop path. JavaScript equivalents exist in js/wield.js, js/objnam.js, and js/do.js; preserve their state and drop admission contracts.

Message sequencing is source-significant: topl.c:update_topl() invokes more() when glibr() prints the second message while the grease message occupies the line. Keep the turn caller in source order and let the existing TTY path receive both messages.
